html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. API: application programming interface; SDK: software development kit; MCP: Model Context Protocol

  • Three ways to construct an agent: a custom loop on the API, the Claude Agent SDK, and Claude Managed Agents
  • What a harness is and what it must do
  • Deployment models: self-hosted versus Anthropic-hosted
  • Hooks for deterministic actions
  • Safety limits for runaway agents

2Choosing How to Build

Running case

Tidewater's Overnight Investigator

  • The team wants an agent that investigates suspicious claims for hours, reads files, runs checks and writes a report
  • Requirements: compliance (data stays in Tidewater's cloud), audit logs, and a small team with little time for infrastructure

Option What you get You provide Choose it when
Custom loop on the Messages API Direct model access, fine-grained control The loop, tool execution, context management, retries, permissions, logging Unusual requirements, or you must control every call
Claude Agent SDK The same agent loop and built-in tools as Claude Code, as a Python or TypeScript library, with subagents, hooks, sessions and permissions Hosting and operations You want a proven harness but control over where it runs
Claude Managed Agents (beta) A pre-built agent harness on managed infrastructure with sandboxes, built-in prompt caching and compaction Agent definition and application integration Long-running or asynchronous work with little infrastructure effort
Exam tip

"Long-running, asynchronous, minimal infrastructure" → Managed Agents. "Own the loop and every call" → custom loop. "Claude's harness, hosted by us" → Agent SDK.

The harness

The harness is everything around the model: the loop, tool execution, permissions, context management (pruning, compaction), retries and limits, logging, and session state. Building your own harness gives control but costs effort and risk; the SDK and Managed Agents supply one.

3Agent SDK Essentials

options = ClaudeAgentOptions(
    allowed_tools=["Read", "Grep", "Glob"],     # tools that need no approval prompt
    max_turns=20,                                # safety limit on the loop
    hooks={"PreToolUse": [HookMatcher(matcher="Bash", hooks=[block_dangerous])]},
)
async for message in query(prompt="Review claim 4471 for fraud signals", options=options):
    ...
  • Built-in tools (Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob, web tools) and custom tools or MCP servers can be added; subagents are defined in code or files.
  • The loop ends when the model replies with no tool calls; a result message carries the outcome (success or a limit such as maximum turns or budget).
  • Permissions: allow lists, deny lists and permission modes control what runs without approval.
  • Sessions can be resumed or forked (see the Architect course for detail).
Exam tip

Ask who should run the harness: you (custom loop or Agent SDK) or Anthropic (Managed Agents), then weigh control against effort.

4Managed Agents and Deployment Models

Concept What it is
Agent The model, system prompt, tools, MCP servers and skills
Environment Where sessions run: an Anthropic-managed cloud sandbox, or a self-hosted sandbox on your infrastructure
Session A running agent instance doing a task
Events The messages between your application and the agent (user turns, tool results, status updates)
  • Self-hosted versus Anthropic-hosted: an Anthropic-managed sandbox minimizes infrastructure work; a self-hosted sandbox keeps execution in your own environment for compliance or data-residency needs.
  • Managed Agents provide caching and compaction in the harness. Sessions are stateful and their transcripts persist until you delete them [Verify live].

[Verify live] Claude Managed Agents is a beta feature on the Claude API (and available with some differences on partner platforms). Check the overview page for current models, platforms and limits. As of 8 November 2026.

5Hooks and Safety Limits

  • Hooks are code that runs at fixed points of the agent loop, outside the model: before a tool runs (PreToolUse: allow, deny or rewrite), after a tool returns (PostToolUse: log, transform), on prompt submit, on stop and more.
  • Use hooks for deterministic actions: block destructive commands, enforce policy, redact secrets from tool output, write an audit log. Prompts alone cannot guarantee these.
  • Safety limits for runaway agents: maximum turns, budget caps, timeouts, allow and deny lists, and sandboxing.

Exam tip

A rule that must always hold (never run a destructive command, never log a secret) is a hook or permission rule, not a prompt sentence.

6Exam Q&A

S1Tidewater needs an agent that works for hours asynchronously with very little infrastructure effort. Which option fits best?

  • AA browser extension
  • BClaude Managed Agents
  • CA custom loop with your own sandbox, queue and state store
  • DA single synchronous Messages API call
Show the answer

Answer: B. Managed Agents provide a ready harness and sandboxes for long-running, asynchronous work.

S2A team must keep agent code execution inside its own cloud for compliance. Which deployment model fits?

  • ARunning the agent on a developer laptop that stays inside the office
  • BA self-hosted sandbox environment for the agent
  • CAny Anthropic-managed cloud sandbox
  • DDisabling tools
Show the answer

Answer: B. Self-hosted sandboxes run on your infrastructure for compliance and residency needs.

S3What does the Claude Agent SDK give a developer?

  • AA way to train models
  • BA replacement for evals
  • CA hosted web interface only, with no way to run your own code
  • DThe agent loop and tools of Claude Code as a library you host
Show the answer

Answer: D. The SDK packages Claude's own harness as a Python or TypeScript library.

S4Which task is best handled by a hook rather than a prompt instruction?

  • ASuggesting a good length for the summary that the agent writes at the end
  • BChoosing synonyms
  • CPreventing the agent from running rm -rf on shared storage under any circumstances
  • DAsking for a friendly tone
Show the answer

Answer: C. A destructive-action guarantee needs deterministic enforcement outside the model.

S5An agent occasionally loops far too long and costs rise. Which controls help most?

  • AA much longer system prompt that tells the agent to stop looping
  • BA higher temperature
  • CMore tools
  • DA maximum-turns limit, a budget cap and timeouts
Show the answer

Answer: D. Limits cap runaway behavior regardless of what the model decides.

S6What belongs to the harness of an agent?

  • AOnly the prompt text, because the model does everything else by itself
  • BOnly the model weights
  • COnly the user interface
  • DThe loop, tool execution, permissions, context management, retries and logging
Show the answer

Answer: D. The harness is everything around the model that makes it work as an agent.

S7In Managed Agents, which concept defines where sessions run?

  • AEvents, the messages sent between the app and the agent
  • BPrompt
  • CSchema
  • DEnvironment
Show the answer

Answer: D. The environment is the cloud or self-hosted sandbox in which sessions execute.

S8Why might a team build a custom loop on the Messages API instead of using the SDK?

  • ACustom loops are always cheaper
  • BIt needs fine-grained control over every call and loop step
  • CThe SDK cannot call tools, so a custom loop is the only way to use them
  • DCustom loops need no testing
Show the answer

Answer: B. A custom loop trades effort for full control.

S9Which TWO are valid uses of hooks in an agent? Select TWO.

  • AGuarantee the model's reasoning is correct
  • BRedact secrets from tool output before the model sees it
  • CRemove the need for permissions
  • DBlock tool calls that match a destructive pattern
  • EReplace the model with a smaller one automatically
Show the answer

Answer: B, D. Hooks intercept calls and results deterministically; they do not choose models, guarantee reasoning or replace permissions.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Build options Custom loop (full control) · Agent SDK (Claude's harness as a library) · Managed Agents (managed harness, long-running work)
Harness Loop, tool execution, permissions, context management, retries, logging, state
Managed Agents Agent · Environment (cloud or self-hosted sandbox) · Session · Events; beta
Hosting Anthropic-managed = least effort; self-hosted = compliance and residency
Hooks PreToolUse (allow, deny, rewrite), PostToolUse (log, transform); deterministic
Limits Max turns, budget, timeouts, permissions, sandboxing
